module_description: Comprehensive analysis of atmospheric hazards affecting flight safety, including turbulence, icing, convection, and visibility restrictions. Focuses on operational forecasting and risk assessment for aviation meteorologists.
competencies: Identify and forecast various types of atmospheric turbulence and wind shear
Assess aircraft icing risk based on thermodynamic profiles and cloud characteristics
Predict convective development and associated severe weather hazards
Evaluate factors contributing to fog and haze for visibility forecasting
Determine cloud base and top altitudes for flight planning and terminal operations

learning_objectives: Distinguish between mechanical, convective, and clear-air turbulence (CAT)
Identify synoptic and mesoscale features associated with severe mountain waves
Explain the formation and hazards of wake vortices
Forecast low-level wind shear and microburst conditions during takeoff and landing
visual_elements_needed: Diagram of mountain wave structures including rotors and lenticular clouds
Cross-section of a jet stream showing regions of maximum shear and CAT
Illustration of wake vortex propagation and decay

learning_objectives: Explain the physics of supercooled large droplets (SLD) in icing formation
Differentiate between rime, glaze, and mixed icing based on temperature and drop size
Analyze tephigrams to identify layers of critical icing potential
Interpret WAFS icing potential products for flight path safety assessment
visual_elements_needed: Diagram comparing ice accumulation profiles (Rime vs Glaze) on a wing
Annotated tephigram showing a 'critical layer' for icing
Freezing rain formation process in a warm frontal structure
external_imagery_needed: Photograph of severe icing on an aircraft leading edge or windshield

learning_objectives: Identify the life cycle stages of a Cumulonimbus (CB) cell
Describe the internal dynamics of severe convective updrafts and downdrafts
Predict secondary hazards such as lightning, hail, and squall lines
Evaluate convective potential using stability indices
visual_elements_needed: CB life cycle diagram (Developing, Mature, Dissipating)
Schematic of a multi-cell storm structure
external_imagery_needed: Satellite image of a Mesoscale Convective System (MCS)
Photograph of an anvil cloud (Cb capillatus incus)

learning_objectives: Classify types of fog (radiation, advection, upslope) by formation mechanism
Identify the critical meteorological factors for fog onset and dissipation
Assess the impact of aerosol concentration and humidity on haze development
Interpret RVR (Runway Visual Range) trends in low-visibility conditions
visual_elements_needed: Formation mechanism diagrams for radiation and advection fog
Graph showing visibility vs. relative humidity for different aerosol types

learning_objectives: Estimate cloud base heights using temperature and dew point depressions
Determine cloud top altitudes from satellite imagery and sounding data
Forecast cloud coverage and layer thickness for aviation planning
Apply local topographical knowledge to sub-grid cloud formation
visual_elements_needed: Thermodynamic diagram showing LCL and cloud layer determination
Satellite IR vs. Visible comparison for cloud top identification

module_quiz.description: Summative assessment covering in-flight hazards, icing, convection, and visibility forecasting.
